proposed_facts.reason: The table assigns this inert collision callback to actor index 1, whose animation implements star firing, not initial startup.
The complete collision body ignores its argument and returns false; the corrected state index matches the table.
Collision has no mutations or guards; firing and completion decisions reside in the paired animation callback.
The shared startup helper calls it_80272860 before testing x24 and decrements x24 on its false path. Only the wrapper's transition work is conditional.
Canonical startup physics performs a mutable shared update and enters state 0 with effect-hitlag setup only upon completion.
it_80275158 writes lifetime and scaled half-life timers. The caller supplies attribute x0, clears command variable 2, initializes state/effect, and sets facing-relative yaw.

The actual caller supplies this event through startup collision to the floor-contact branch. The registry has no destroyed handler; the replacement is appropriately descriptive rather than an original-name claim.
The empty void(Item_GObj*) definition and terrain callback invocation establish an unused active-actor argument, not an object necessarily being destroyed.
Common terrain processing surrounds the empty floor-contact event; neither its body nor the actor registry supports a destruction role.
The random bound is cast to s32, the returned integer is cast to f32 before adding x18, and approach pre-decrements the stored countdown.
The exact expression adds an integer random offset to a floating base without validating bounds, so integer-valued delay is not guaranteed.
Both state-1 entry and animation refresh install the same empty accessory event.
The two installation sites and false animation-status guard match the proposal; the accessory event itself is unconditionally empty.

prev_pos receives configured offsets, while it_8026BB88 independently computes pos from the actor and ECB midpoint. Descriptor fields, single allocation attempt, and success-only directional audio match canonical code.
Every setter invocation writes 1 and returns false. Projectile animation decrements and stores lifetime before either termination test.

The actor follows indices 2→0→1, distinct from animation identifier -1. Target absence suppresses firing work without directly terminating; allocation failure does not roll back caller mutations. Projectile lifetime and command-flag ordering also match.

contradictions.reason: Accepted deferral for all three .sdata2 claims: source demonstrates literal uses but cannot establish compiled size, pool membership, placement, immutability, or load form. No compiled-layout correction is proposed.
The three collision claims incorrectly described index 1 as the first motion phase. The proposal preserves the supported no-op behavior and identifies the firing phase precisely.
The two startup-physics claims omitted mutations performed while the shared helper returns false. The proposed explanations correctly separate shared update work from guarded transition work.
The projectile spawn purpose incorrectly called x0 a launch parameter. Its resolved callee initializes lifetime timers, supporting the correction.

The Destroyed name, destruction-specific argument interpretation, and destruction purpose relied on adjacency. Actual registration and the caller chain support an empty startup floor-contact event instead.
The two delay claims misstated conversion order and guaranteed an integer-valued result. Canonical code converts the random integer before adding the floating base.
The two accessory explanations used misleading first-motion wording and omitted initial installation. Both state-1 entry and refresh install the empty event.
The spawn data-flow claim conflated offset prev_pos with independently computed pos. The correction preserves both descriptor outputs and allocation/audio branches.
The termination-flag explanation implied a single 0→1 transition and conditional lifetime decrement. Repeated writes are possible, and lifetime is always decremented before flag inspection.

The file-level summary incorrectly treated target absence and interval expiration as independent termination conditions. The corrected summary preserves count consumption, target-null behavior, and failed-allocation side effects.
